Continuous monitoring is required under the amended Law of 12 November 2004. Screening must be documented and retainable for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any language but must be written in Latin alphabet characters and rendered, if necessary, in a transliteration into French, German, or Luxembourgish. The name must include or be followed by 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' as the mandatory legal form indicator. The name must be distinguishable from names of existing entities and pending reservations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission de surveillance du secteur financier
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Business Registers registrar within 15 days of the rejection notification. The appeal must set out the grounds for challenging the rejection, attach the initial reservation receipt, and offer the proposed name in alternative transliterations. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may submit a formal petition to the administrative tribunal of Luxembourg. During the appeal process, the name reservation window is tolled. If the reservation expires without a final decision, a new reservation may be filed without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole registered office. Luxembourg law requires a physical registered office in Luxembourg with a visible sign, supervision, and access to corporate books and records. A virtual office may only be used as a supplementary administrative facility

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Book III - Titles I and IV, notably Articles 710-1 to 710-24 (SARL provisions); Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq.; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the RESA electronic gazette.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) in coordination with the District Court of Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif notarié) incorporating the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts), filed electronically on Form A (Demande d'inscription au RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital is EUR 12,000. At incorporation, the full capital must be subscribed and at least 5% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up in cash before signature of the notarial deed. The paid-up funds must be deposited into a blocked 'company in formation' (SARL en formation) bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution or held in notary escrow; the bank or notary issues a capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) which is released only upon registration of the company with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators and sole shareholder of [COMPANY NAME] Société à Responsabilité Limitée hereby approve: 1. The subscription to the entire share capital as set out in the notarized articles of incorporation, acknowledgment of the paid-up portion on behalf of the company, and release of the blocked capital account to the company's registered accounts; 2. Adoption of the registered office at [ADDRESS], L-1118 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; 3. Appointment of [NAME] as Manager (Gérant) with sole signature authority, and of [NAME] as approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if legally required; 4. Authorization of the notary to file the deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and to publish the notice in the RESA electronic gazette. Adopted under the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Pre-Incorporation Legal Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online name search portal; Notary's office (Etude de Notaire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to run an RCS screening for the proposed corporate name to confirm availability and distinguishability, validate the legal form (SARL), confirm the registered office address acceptability (leased or owned premises), and verify that the telematics/logistics SaaS activity is lawful and compatible with the corporate object clause. The notary then drafts the notarized articles of incorporation in French, including the corporate object, share capital structure, manager powers, and registered office clause.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and three alternates
Draft Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) in French
Corporate object description (ISIC 6201 / logistics telematics SaaS)
Identity documents (passport) of shareholders and proposed managers
Draft power of attorney for the notary, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or found confusingly similar, the notary files a revised name selection immediately; no waiting period applies, and a new RCS screening is performed within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or notary escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of 'SARL en formation' and deposit at least 5% of each share's nominal value (minimum EUR 600 against the EUR 12,000 capital) via wire transfer from the shareholder. Provide the bank with corporate KYC documentation and obtain a capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, confirming the deposit and the irrevocable blocking until RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Passport and proof of residential address of each subscriber
Beneficial ownership declaration and source of funds evidence
Draft statuts and provisional corporate object
Bank account opening forms for the entity in formation
Shareholders' resolution approving the capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening, engage an alternative Luxembourg bank or request the notary to hold the funds in escrow; the notary issues a substitute blocking certificate, and the incorporation timeline is extended by up to five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscribing shareholders (or their attorney-in-fact) appear before the notary, verify the final French text of the statuts, acknowledge receipt and payment of the paid-up portion, and sign the notarial deed. The notary verifies legal capacity, absence of disqualifications, compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915, and the adequacy of the capital blocking certificate. The deed is read aloud, signed by all parties and the notary, and the notary then delivers a certified copy (expédition) for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Blocking certificate from bank or notary escrow
Proof of registered office address (lease or landlord's written consent)
Identity documents of all subscribers and managers (originals)
Draft statuts approved by subscribers
Beneficial ownership register declaration data (RBE - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the capital certificate or identity documentation, the notary issues a formal notice; the defect is cured within three business days by obtaining a corrected certificate or supplemental notarized clarification before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - Electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically files Form A (demande d'inscription), attaching the certified copy of the notarial deed, the signed statuts, and the identity data of the managers, within one month of signature. The RCS verifies the legal form, object, capital, and registered office; upon approval, the company is registered and receives an RCS number and LEI-referenced identification, and legal personality is acquired as of that registration date.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial expédition of the deed of incorporation
RCS Form A signed by the notary
Articles of Incorporation in French (certified)
Identification of managers (criminal record extract and proof of civil capacity)
Statement of registered office and domiciliation agreement, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément d'information), the notary submits the supplementary documents or clarifies the deed within 15 days; if the query is not cured, the application may be re-filed with a corrected deed, and any contested refusal can be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court under the Law of 19 December 2002.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA Electronic Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) / Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary, simultaneously with or immediately after RCS registration, transmits the statutory publication file to LBR for insertion in RESA. The publication includes the company's capitalization, object, registered office, managers' names, and date of deed. LBR issues a publication confirmation, which constitutes the formal notice to third parties and must occur within one month of the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Certified summary of incorporation as drafted by the notary
RCS registration confirmation number
Notary's transmission certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or rejected, the notary rectifies the transmitted data and re-submits within 48 hours; if the deadline is missed, the company may apply to the court for an order to accept late publication, without prejudice to good-faith third-party protections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security, and Establishment Permit Post-Registration Matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des PME; Commune of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of registration, apply online for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (if taxable supplies are anticipated) using the standard registration form, register the company with the ACD for corporate income tax (form 1), register with the CCSS as employer upon first hiring, and file for the municipal business tax through the commune. For the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement), submit an exemption declaration confirming that the ISIC 6201 software and telematics SaaS activity is not an enumerated regulated trade; obtain the Ministry's written exemption confirmation.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and LEI confirmation
Notarized statuts in French
Proof of registered office and lease
Manager's identity and criminal record (EU/third-country version)
Declaration of activities for the establishment permit exemption
Bank account details and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or corporate tax registration is queried, respond to the AEDT/ACD with corrected forms within 10 days; if the establishment permit exemption is refused, file an administrative reclamation with the Minister of the Economy within one month and subsequently appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale des PME (Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) - statutory exemption confirmed for ISIC 6201 computer programming and software activities; no industrial or physical operating permit is required for office-based fleet telematics SaaS operations under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to crafts, trades, and independent professions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency - AEV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt (no EIA mandatory) - the software and logistics-telematics data processing activity is not listed in Annexes IV or V of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no environmental permit is triggered for office premises, server rooms, or data-center support facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to manufacturing discharge; general obligations apply: compliance with the Law of 19 December 2008 on water management for any sanitary wastewater discharge, the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management for e-waste and WEEE-compliant disposal of end-of-life hardware, and the EU Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency in Data Centres for server infrastructure; VOC threshold reporting under Directive 2010/75/EU is not triggered for this activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the registered office premises from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS), including evacuation plans, smoke detectors, and extinguisher compliance; structural load and building occupancy inspection by the Commune of Luxembourg's building authority for the leased office floor; workplace health and safety clearance pursuant to the Law of 17 June 1994 on labour safety and health, validated by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), covering workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and a documented risk assessment for telematics and dispatch operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Official portals: MyGuichet.lu and eCDF (electronic correspondence and filing platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Luxembourg SARL: (1) Incorporate before a Luxembourg notary and file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) to obtain the national business registration number; (2) apply to the AEDT for the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) either via MyGuichet.lu or with a paper Form 640/640ADR; (3) the ACD allocates the direct tax file number (matricule) upon registration of the corporate income tax liability; (4) an entity established outside the EU must appoint a jointly and severally liable Luxembourg VAT representative (représentant responsable solidaire); (5) if the company makes EU distance sales or B2C electronic services, register for the OSS/IOSS scheme via MyGuichet.lu. Administrative filings are accepted in French, German, and, for specific portals, English.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box. Available elections: (a) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 VAT Law; (b) fiscal unity affiliation for corporate income tax under Article 164bis LIR requiring a 95% direct or indirect holding; (c) election to waive the small-enterprise VAT exemption under Article 57 VAT Law (turnover threshold EUR 35,000) and instead be regularly taxed; (d) OSS / non-EU scheme election for qualifying e-services and distance sales; (e) entity classification of hybrid entities follows LIR Article 159 and the MLI / treaty provisions, with elections in limited cases for transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for established small enterprises (Article 57 VAT Law); zero threshold for non-established foreign entities, which are mandatorily registrable from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, CTC reporting, or digital stamping is in force for B2B invoices. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies to central government and public-sector buyers using the PEPPOL network (Peppol BIS 3.0). B2B and B2C invoices must comply with Articles 75-78 VAT Law and be retained for 10 years. VIES recapitulative statements must be filed monthly where intra-EU supplies exceed EUR 50,000 per quarter, otherwise quarterly. Intrastat dispatch declarations apply where annual intra-EU dispatches exceed the EUR 460,000 threshold. OSS/IOSS returns are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu. Cross-border B2B invoices must state the customer's valid VAT ID and the reverse-charge legal basis.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export supplies to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT (Article 43 VAT Law); intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-identified customer qualify for 0% VAT (Article 42 VAT Law) conditional on VIES validation and recapitulative statement. Services: freight and logistics services directly connected to the export or import of goods, including fleet dispatch and handling operations, qualify for 0% (Article 44 VAT Law). For the SaaS/telematics scope: B2B supplies of fleet route optimization and telematics services to non-established customers fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the general place-of-supply rule (customer location, Article 44 EU VAT Directive); no Luxembourg VAT is chargeable and the customer applies reverse charge. B2C e-services to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's Member State via OSS; B2C e-services to non-EU consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CMR waybill or AWB air waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 payment proof
VIES electronic validation extract of customer VAT ID
Contract or purchase order governing provision of services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and ACD may conduct retrospective audits up to 7 years for VAT/corporate tax (extended to 10 years in case of fraud or wilful tax evasion). Where export zero-rating is applied but the statutory documentation bundle is defective, the VAT exemption is clawed back retroactively with late-payment interest at 0.6% per month and administrative fines between EUR 250 and EUR 12,500 (Article 91 VAT Law). Aggravated VAT fraud is punishable by fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years (Articles 92-93 VAT Law); the fraud or abuse of law doctrine (fraus legis) allows recharacterization of artificial arrangements. The invoice issuer is jointly and severally liable for VAT shown on an invoice (Article 67 VAT Law). Under transfer-pricing principles, intercompany receivables unresolved beyond approximately 180 days may be recharacterized as loans or deemed distributions of profit, with additional income assessed at CIT/MBT rates and late-payment penalties under the General Tax Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign exchange administrative supervision is shared with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for regulatory policy matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a euro-area Member State, has full current and capital account convertibility. There are no legal restrictions on currency conversion between EUR and foreign currencies, no central bank prior-approval requirements for dividend payments, and no capital controls on profit repatriation. The freedom of capital movements is guaranteed under TFEU Article 63. The only practical frictions are AML/KYC onboarding due diligence, EU/UN sanctions screening, and the statutory withholding tax treatment for certain passive income (e.g., 15% withholding on interest and royalty payments under national law). These frictions are not exchange-control hurdles and are contractually mitigable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory rules in Luxembourg requiring surrender of export proceeds or mandatory conversion of foreign-currency receipts into EUR. Receipts from international sales may be held in the currencies of contract settlement or voluntarily converted through the banking market. Invoicing in EUR or USD is permitted without central bank reporting; however, banks must record balance-of-payments statistics under BCL/Eurosystem monetary and payment reporting requirements where the transaction exceeds the BCL's reporting threshold (typically EUR 250,000 for a single non-cash operation).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High only for non-escrowed, day-to-day treasury flows. A Luxembourg-authorized or EU-passported e-money institution (EMI) may be used for receivables collection and supplier payments because EMIs are regulated under the Luxembourg law implementing Directive 2009/110/EC. Legal constraints: the EMI cannot hold a company's statutory initial capital as a notary-recognized escrow (only a credit institution can); EMIs may not grant credit or provide full corporate banking guarantees; cross-border onboarding of an EU EMI often triggers equivalent AML/KYC checks; and reliance on a single EMI creates correspondent banking concentration risk for larger FX transactions. The structure should therefore pair an EMI rail with a tier-1 licensed bank for capital escrow and substantial FX conversions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute Luxembourg statutory mandate requiring all directors to appear physically for bank account opening; however, in practice, for a newly formed SARL with non-resident ownership and no significant operational footprint, the managing director or the majority UBO must typically attend an in-person interview in Luxembourg (or before a Luxembourg consular delegate abroad). Remote opening is accepted by several tier-1 banks only where an eIDAS-certified qualified electronic signature is used, or where the application is made through a Luxembourg-regulated professional (notary or audit, tax and accounting firm) maintaining an existing delegation agreement with the bank. The CSSF AML Law requires reliable, independent-source identification of all signatories and UBOs; a physical meeting remains the predominant, legally cleanest evidence for a non-resident-owned SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident presence of the sole director/UBO in a non-EU jurisdiction classified as higher-risk or strategically deficient in AML/CFT
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy legalized/apostilled; proof of residential address via utility bill or bank statement; official board resolution appointing a Luxembourg alternate director; group corporate-organigram; tax residence certificates issued by the foreign tax authority; a 12-month source-of-funds file from the originating bank; a notarized charter and articles of association; an Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) declaration; and a Criminal Records Certificate from the country of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection source or subscriber funds cannot be explained or are held in a private/asset-holding vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share subscription deed; bank-to-bank reference letter from the remitting institution; audited financial statements or certified opening balance-sheet; bank statements demonstrating fund provenance (12 months); source-of-funds questionnaire; anti-money-laundering declaration of the subscriber; LEI certificate; and a notarial capital-attestation for the deposit of minimum share capital (either EUR 12,000 in cash or in-kind valuation certified by a statutory auditor).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or media-sanctions hit on a UBO or director, requiring risk escalation by the bank's compliance department
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full risk-assessment report prepared by a licensed compliance advisory; clear rationale and documentation eliminating false hits; cluster screening results using World-Check/LexisNexis or equivalent; an independent legal opinion on the PEP status and reputational risk; signed declaration of no ongoing criminal or regulatory investigation; and a documented funding-route map illustrating legitimate commercial business income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient commercial substance for a software company focusing on fleet dispatch with telematics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client contracts and SaaS licensing agreements; invoices for subscription services; payroll and subcontractor proof for Luxembourg operations; lease or commercial office agreements; statutory filings at the RCS showing ISIC 6201 activity; and a cash-flow forecast demonstrating acceptable bank-account velocity and operating expenses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The qualifying inbound routing for a share capital injection is a SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer initiated from the shareholder's own account. The transmitter must use the statistical purpose code 'B' (capital contribution) or, where required, refer to 'Increase in share capital' and the contract reference. The bank will require a notarized board/EGM decision, the share subscription deed, identification by name of each contributing shareholder, and an attested deposit letter for the notarial file. Funds must be cleared by the respondent bank of the Luxembourg credit institution, and the bank will complete BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting as required under the Eurosystem framework. Any financing from related parties should be documented as shareholder loan or equity; the latter is notified as direct foreign investment and is freely resettable under EU capital-movement rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For routine EU supplier payments, SEPA Credit Transfer is the lowest-cost rail. For international settlement of technology, telematics hardware procurement and logistics services, SWIFT MT103 with proper purpose code 'Trade in services' is the standard; high-value or documentary imports of hardware should be settled through a commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) with a Luxembourg bank confirming the LC, accompanied by transport documents, commercial invoices and authenticity certificates. For recurring SaaS subscription collection and marketpay flows, Stripe Billing may be integrated via a payment institution or through the bank's merchant acquiring gateway; nevertheless, direct MT103 remains the substantive treasury clearing instrument for larger counterparties. All outbound transfers must be subject to sanctions screening and match the underlying contract; no cash settlements are permissible in excess of EUR 10,000 without facilitated traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla foreign-exchange forwards with regulated Luxembourg/EU credit institutions under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a local foreign-exchange framework
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for balancing EUR/USD or EUR/CHF liquidity arising from fleet SaaS and telematics royalties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-fully-convertible counterparty currencies, executed only for non-speculative underlying trade flows
European-style currency options (puts/calls) for asymmetric hedging when fee income is exposed to currency movements, subject to MiFID II suitability and risk-management proof
Spot currency transactions for immediate settlement of dividend pre-funding or operational account concentration rebalancing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial accounts (balance sheet, income statement, annexed notes) filed with the RCS and published in the RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000 per instance plus potential daily fines; persistent non-filing triggers compulsory winding-up proceedings and possible strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) confirmation declaration filed in the Luxembourg RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) administered by the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the RBE registration anniversary; UBO changes must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 500 to EUR 1,250 for non-compliance; intentional failure may result in fines up to EUR 5,000 and imprisonment; continued default may lead to judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax return for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 September following the tax year for a 31 December year-end; extensions are available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 25,000; statutory interest on outstanding tax; tax authorities may estimate the taxable base and issue enforcement orders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation and final periodic VAT return (or annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final monthly or quarterly VAT return of the tax year due by the 15th of the month following the relevant period; annual reconciliation accompanies the final return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% on unpaid VAT; late filing penalties up to EUR 750 per month; arrears interest applies

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three small-company thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce of 50 employees; audit is also compulsory for public-interest entities, credit institutions, and insurance undertakings
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Accounting Law of 19 December 2002 as amended; IFRS mandatory for public-interest entities and optional for other companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain an accurate UBO file in the RBE; any UBO change must be filed within 30 days and an annual confirmation declaration is due each year within 30 days of the RBE registration anniversary
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholders' general meetings and management decisions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (17.00% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City; rate varies with the commune of the registered office)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box: 80% exemption for qualifying IP-derived income, yielding a 5.01% effective maximum rate; R&D tax credit of up to 20% of qualifying research and development expenditure; digitalization investment tax credit up to 12%; start-up guarantee for first eight years; loss carryforward is unlimited (0 in the numeric field indicates no statutory expiry); participation exemption fully exempts qualifying dividend and capital gains from Luxembourg tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (Déclaration collective pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, d'impôt commercial communal au Luxembourg) filed exclusively online through the eCDF portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); simultaneous filing of the net wealth tax return (form 105) is required for SARLs
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is the last day of the sixth month after the fiscal year-end (for a calendar-year SARL: 30 June); extensions can be requested via eCDF, and for electronic filers without professional help the ACD frequently tolerates filing until 31 December; quarterly CIT prepayments are due on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August and 10 November

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax identification number (matricule), registered office, date of incorporation, legal form code for SARL
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL filing because of a Luxembourg permanent establishment must insert the PE address and PE matricule; the head-office foreign tax number must not be listed as Luxembourg tax number

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet summary: total fixed assets, financial fixed assets, cash and receivables, total equity and debt; figures must bridge to the statutory annual accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents using home-state GAAP must attach a reconciliation to Luxembourg GAAP/IFRS and show the net worth allocated to the Luxembourg PE through a permanent establishment draw table

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: net commercial profit, adjustments for non-deductible expenses (including 25% of interest paid to related lenders), exempt dividend/royalty income under the participation exemption or IP box, and loss carryforward claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE's taxable income must be calculated under the Authorized OECD Approach-like profit attribution: allocate capital against risks and functions; intercompany invoicing must be supported by transfer pricing documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (ICC) add-backs and allowances: add-back of 25% of net interest expense, 5% of related-party royalty payments, and deduction of the municipal capital allowance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must apportion movable fixed assets to the commune of the PE based on permanent installation; receivables from the head office may be excluded to avoid double allocation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments: R&D and digital credit declarations, foreign tax credit, and state of quarterly CIT prepayments made by the SARL
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities cannot claim domestic tax credits for activities exercised abroad unless covered by a non-discrimination clause; recovery of foreign withholding tax is made by filing the corresponding refund form with the ACD

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing annex: list of related-party transactions, method used (CUP, resale, cost plus, TNMM, profit split), and indication whether a Local File exists
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Annex TP must include a functional analysis of the Luxembourg PE and the allocation of profits on outbound logistics-fleet dispatch services performed for or by the foreign parent

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a per-month surcharge of €250 for a SARL, plus monthly interest on the outstanding tax at 0.6%; deliberate non-filing after formal notice leads to an ex officio assessment with a 50% increase of tax due; for an estimate-only return, a 25% increase is common. Criminal fines of up to €25,000 apply to directors involved in wilful failure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (Luxembourg withholding tax on distributed profits of a SARL, irrespective of the recipient being resident or non-resident); the rate is reduced to 0% for a qualifying corporate shareholder under the Luxembourg participation exemption if the parent holds 10% for at least 12 months; liquidation distributions outside subscribed capital are not subject to WHT
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke an income tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must submit an original or certified tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, certifying residence in the treaty state, and a declaration of share ownership; the TRC must be presented to the Luxembourg paying agent at or before payment to apply the treaty withholding rate ex ante. If the full 15% rate has been withheld, the recipient files a refund claim with the ACD using the official dividend WHT recovery form (usually Form 500/501) and must enclose a copy of the TRC, proof of underlying tax withheld, and a legal opinion if the treaty benefit is based on a beneficial-ownership argument
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties (0%), and no domestic withholding tax on outward interest payments to non-residents, except for interest payments with a profit-participating character which are treated as dividends. Under typical Luxembourg tax treaties, royalty withholding rates are 0% (e.g., the 2024 Luxembourg-Netherlands treaty) and interest withholding rates range from 0% to 10% (0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive when a 25% ownership threshold is met); all exemptions require a valid TRC and an economic-substance attestation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold applies to related-party transactions below EUR 1 million; tax administration expects a Local File when annual related-party operating transactions exceed EUR 1 million or when related-party financing exceeds EUR 500,000. Groups with consolidated annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more must file a Master File, Local File and CbCR notification (due at the end of the reporting month after the fiscal-year end)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the EU ATAD general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) and the Luxembourg 'wholly artificial arrangement' doctrine: corporate residency, management and control, and real operational substance must be present in Luxembourg. A SARL operating in the logistics-tech sector must demonstrate, through employment records and invoices, that dispatch/optimization algorithms are really managed locally; otherwise, the ACD can disregard the entity for treaty purposes. There is no separate ESR annual filing similar to the UAE regime, but substance is policed via the RBE beneficial-owner register, CbCR, and transfer pricing examinations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of SaaS subscription revenues from fleet-dispatch operations, creation of fictitious invoices for trip fees, round-tripping digital payments between the SARL and a sister entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction, or destruction of electronic accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under the LIR at the full CIT rate of 24.94% plus monetary tax interest at 0.6% per month; criminal conviction carries a fine of up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of one to five years (Article 396 LIR); tax fraud also triggers the loss of all deductions and protection against arbitrary audits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute or approve the fraudulent scheme are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax shortfall under Luxembourg civil law; in practice the ACD issues travel bans, freezing orders on personal bank accounts, and may seize director assets, and imprisonment is imposed on the natural person rather than the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL is only a letterbox entity: no employees in Luxembourg, no local bank account, the fleet-dispatch software is fully developed abroad, agreements and board decisions are executed abroad, but the company still claims tax treaty benefits or EU directive rate or uses the 80% IP box exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty and directive benefits; all IP licence income is reassessed at 24.94% CIT with a 50% non-disclosure surcharge under Section 190 (5) of the Luxembourg Tax Abatement Law; the Luxembourg RCS can open liquidation proceedings; a Shell-company finding makes the entity unbankable for payment rails such as Stripe Billing and wire transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors who allow the company to operate without genuine substance are jointly liable for the additional assessments and fines; repeated violations constitute the criminal offence of mismanagement under the Commercial Companies Law (Article 1800-1), carrying personal liability, asset confiscation and a ban from running companies for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify, document and file the ultimate beneficial owner(s) in the RBE register, absence of KYC files on the shareholders owning logistics-fleet data or receiving dividend distributions, or issuance of bearer-like ownership in the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE administrative fines of EUR 100 to EUR 500 per day of non-compliance, and criminal fines up to EUR 1.25 million; the law 12 November 2004 (as amended) gives the prosecution power to impose imprisonment up to five years for aggravated AML; payments through Stripe Billing may be frozen by PayPal/Stripe due to the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for AML deficiencies; under Luxembourg law 24 July 2015, a director who fails to alert the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) is subject to criminal sanction; travel bans and precautionary seizure of property are issued by the investigating judge at the request of the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor.
